title: Sebastian and the Cipher
premise: Sebastian Okoye, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made him the quiet keeper of his small town's secrets, is pulled into a nightmare when the coffin of beloved town founder Elias Wren is exhumed and found empty. As Sebastian digs through ten years of claims files, he realizes the killer is someone who knows the archives better than he does — someone who helped him file them. The cipher hidden in Wren's old insurance ledgers points to a decades-old fraud that built the town on stolen inheritances, and to a survivor who erased their own identity to escape it. In the end, Sebastian traps the killer — his own mentor and archive partner — but must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the last innocent heir, paying the price of survival himself by burning the file that could have made his career.
about_author: Dominic Okonkwo is a former forensic accountant who spent six years untangling inheritance frauds across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about paper trails, buried money, and the people who keep the records no one wants read.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A court order forces the exhumation of founder Elias Wren for an insurance dispute; when the coffin opens, it holds only weighted sandbags. Sebastian's memory flashes to the burial ten years ago. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He returns to the records office where he and his mentor Ruth Calloway have archived every claim in town history, searching the Wren death file. Pages are missing — cut cleanly. Beat: the unsettling realization someone got there first.

chapters.title: The Sandbag Detail
chapters.summary: Sheriff Ilsa Brandt's POV. The sheriff resents Sebastian's involvement but needs his memory; she shows him the sandbags were filled from the cemetery's own soil. Beat: grudging alliance forming over shared unease.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Premiums
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Someone kept paying Wren's life insurance premiums after his death — cash, untraceable. Sebastian recalls filing one such payment and can't remember the payer's face, which has never happened. Beat: first crack in his confidence.

chapters.title: Ruth's Warning
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth urges Sebastian to drop the case, citing the town's fragile peace. Her fear reads as protectiveness but lands strangely specific. Beat: loyalty shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Ledgers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He finds numeric anomalies in Wren's founding-era insurance ledgers — a repeating cipher embedded in premium columns. His photographic mind decodes the first fragment: a name, half-erased. Beat: intellectual thrill curdling into danger.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Mara Villalobos's POV. A sharp-eyed paralegal representing Wren's estate hires on to the case and clashes with Sebastian, then shares her own discovery: Wren had a secret grandchild. Beat: prickly partnership, first spark of trust.

chapters.title: What the Ground Gave Back
chapters.summary: Sheriff Brandt's POV. Forensics dates the coffin tampering to within days of the burial — meaning the body was taken while the whole town mourned. Beat: the killer isn't a stranger; the killer was grieving alongside them.

chapters.title: The Fire at the Annex
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The old records annex burns overnight; Sebastian saves one box on instinct — Wren's original policies. He suspects arson meant for him. Beat: survivor's guilt and sharpened resolve.

chapters.title: Decoding Elias
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Mara's alternating POV. Working through the night, they crack more of the cipher: Wren insured land he never owned, laundering an inheritance stolen from a displaced family. Beat: the town's beloved origin revealed as theft.

chapters.title: The Beneficiary
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The policy's contingent beneficiary is listed under a name that was legally declared dead forty years ago — the displaced family's daughter. Beat: the mystery acquires a human face and a moral weight.

chapters.title: Someone Is Filing Behind Me
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Files he memorized have been subtly altered — dates shifted, initials changed. Only three people ever had full access: him, the sheriff, and Ruth. Beat: paranoia; the archive itself becomes untrustworthy.

chapters.title: Ruth's Alibi
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth produces an airtight alibi for the exhumation window, almost too perfect. She tells Sebastian a partial truth about Wren's final years. Beat: sympathy for Ruth deepening even as doubt grows.

chapters.title: The Grandchild Surfaces
chapters.summary: Sheriff Brandt's POV. The secret grandchild — a middle-aged nurse named Ada — comes forward, terrified, claiming someone left the cipher fragments on her doorstep. Beat: the stakes turn personal and protective.

chapters.title: A Memory That Lies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian discovers a fabricated document bearing his own archival initials — planted evidence implicating him in the coffin theft. Beat: horror as his perfect memory becomes both his defense and his cage.

chapters.title: The Night Visit
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara is attacked in the records office by someone who knows the building's blind spots intimately. She survives and describes a voice, not a face. Beat: fear made physical; the partnership becomes a lifeline.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Sheriff Brandt's POV. Following the cipher's final coordinates, they find Wren's actual remains buried beneath the displaced family's homestead — returned, deliberately, home. Beat: grim reverence; the killer wanted this found.

chapters.title: The Confession File
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Hidden in the box he saved from the fire, Sebastian finds a confession draft in Ruth's handwriting — but dated after her declared stroke left her unable to write. Beat: devastating realization that the confession itself is a plant.

chapters.title: Calloway
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth confronts the true killer — her long-estranged child, the 'dead' daughter's descendant, who infiltrated the archive years ago under a new identity and has been steering Sebastian all along. Beat: maternal love weaponized against complicity.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian baits the killer with a forged cipher fragment only accessible through the archive system, forcing a midnight confrontation in the stacks where the altered files are exposed. Beat: controlled terror; his memory versus their forgery.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Climax, Sebastian's POV. The killer confesses: they took Wren's body to force the town to reckon with its stolen foundation, and killed only when the fire plan went wrong. Ruth takes a fatal blow shielding Sebastian. Beat: grief, fury, and the arrest that feels like losing.

chapters.title: Empty Coffin, Open Book
chapters.summary: Resolution, Sebastian and Mara's POV. Wren is reburied beside the homestead; Ada receives the restored inheritance. Sebastian burns the planted file that would have exonerated him spectacularly but destroyed Ada's claim, choosing the town's healing over his own vindication. Beat: bittersweet peace — survival paid in full.
